subject: Atlas FS RFP — contract exhibits & order form clarifications
messages:
From: Marcus Ellery <m.ellery@atlasfs.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@atlasfs.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Atlas FS RFP — contract exhibits & order form clarifications

Hi Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Legal is working through the RFP packet and we have a handful of follow-ups specifically around the order form exhibit and indemnity/caps language. Can you confirm the following so we can move to our internal procurement review?

1) IP: We need to confirm that all output generated by Redwood for Atlas remains Atlas's data for the purposes of ownership of derivative works created from our inputs. Is there an existing exhibit that clarifies output ownership and usage?

2) Indemnity: We see the standard Redwood indemnity in Exhibit B; Atlas legal is asking if Redwood can accept a mutual indemnity for third-party IP claims that directly result from Atlas-provided training data or prompts.

3) Liability cap: Our procurement team would like to understand your proposed cap for a multi-year commitment. Is there a calendar-year cap you can point us to (we can share our target as well).

4) Order Form: We will need a draft order form that includes committed throughput, region, and service levels. Can you share a draft that includes SLA terms and remedies?

We appreciate a redline or answers in a short doc — our timeline is to present to our procurement committee on Apr 28.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Ellery
Sr. Counsel, Contracts | Atlas Financial Services
[Attachment: Atlas_RFP_Tracker.xlsx (xlsx, 12KB)]

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Ellery <m.ellery@atlasfs.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procure@atlasfs.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Apr 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Atlas FS RFP — contract exhibits & order form clarifications

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear list. I pulled together preliminary answers and attached a short Q&A doc with suggested Exhibit language for IP/Indemnity and a draft order form (order form is high level and we can add committed throughput numbers once you confirm the tier). Highlights below — please see attached for the redlineable text.

- IP: Redwood’s standard position is that customer input and customer data remain the customer’s. For model output, we propose a license to Atlas to use and create derivatives for its internal business purposes; we generally don’t assign moral rights, but we can make the license broad and exclusive for Atlas’s internal use. See section "Output & Use" in the attached.

- Indemnity: We typically provide an IP indemnity for claims alleging infringement by the model code or underlying models we ship. We cannot accept a blanket mutual indemnity for third-party content created from customer prompts (risk of adversarial inputs). However, Redwood can agree to a mutual indemnity limited to direct breaches of confidentiality and proven misuse of Atlas data (i.e., if Atlas supplies proprietary training corpora that Redwood ingests under an explicit training addendum). Suggested wording in the doc.

- Liability cap: For enterprise commitments we’re willing to discuss a blended cap tied to fees (e.g., 1x annual committed spend for routine breaches, higher caps for gross negligence/willful misconduct). I put a placeholder in the Exhibit-C spreadsheet to discuss 1x vs 2x and carve-outs for IP indemnity.

- Order Form/SLA: Attached draft includes throughput tiers, target p95 latency, and standard credits for uptime. We can tailor region-specific SLAs if you plan to run in us-east vs eu-west.

Attached: Redwood_Legal_QA_v1.docx (docx, 38KB), Exhibit-C_Liability_Schedule.xlsx, Atlas_OrderForm_DRAFT.pdf

Let me know if you want to hop on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk legal and procurement through the answers.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: Redwood_Legal_QA_v1.docx (docx, 38KB)]

We uploaded our redline and commentary inline — the key ask is a mutual IP indemnity limited to claims arising from either party’s code or models, and a clarifying carve-out that Atlas content supplied under confidentiality is covered.

I am looping in our procurement lead Samira Chan (samira.chan@atlasfs.com) — she will coordinate committed spend numbers.

Attached: Atlas_OrderForm_DRAFT_redline.pdf (pdf, 45KB)

Regards,
Marcus

Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Atlas FS RFP — contract exhibits & order form clarifications

Mina / Marissa —

Forwarding Marcus's redline and Atlas's comments. Key asks from Atlas legal:
- Mutual IP indemnity limited to claims arising from either party's code/models; Atlas wants confirmation that if they supply proprietary corpora under a training addendum, Redwood will indemnify for third-party claims tied to Redwood's misuse.
- Liability cap: Atlas procurement will propose a committed-spend-linked cap. They asked about 1x vs 2x annual committed spend and exceptions for willful misconduct.
- Order form: They returned a draft with specific throughput numbers and requested that our SLA include region-specific p95 targets and credits.

I suggested an initial position in the attached Q&A (see "Indemnity: proposed carve-outs"). Can legal take a pass on tightened language for the mutual indemnity carve, and commercial can confirm whether 1x annual spend is acceptable for a multi-year reserved capacity deal?

Proposed next steps:
- Mina: provide redline to Exhibit C and proposed training addendum language by EOD Wed (21 Apr).
- Marissa: confirm pricing / committed spend scenarios (1x/2x cap sensitivity) by Wed EOD so I can update the order form.
- If we have alignment, I'll propose a joint call with Atlas legal on Thu morning.

Thanks —
Ben

[Attachment: Atlas_OrderForm_DRAFT_redline.pdf (pdf, 45KB)]

From: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Ellery <m.ellery@atlasfs.com>, Samira Chan <samira.chan@atlasfs.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2026 16:44:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Atlas FS RFP — contract exhibits & order form clarifications

Ben / Marissa —

Thanks for the context — I reviewed Marcus's redline and drafted tightened language for Exhibit C and a short training addendum. High-level positions:

1) Mutual IP indemnity: Acceptable if narrowly scoped. My draft limits mutual indemnity to: (a) claims alleging infringement by either party's pre-existing software or models, and (b) claims directly caused by the other party's breach of the training addendum obligations (including misuse of confidential corpus). It excludes third-party output generated solely by prompts that the customer crafts (we retain our current carve-out for adversarial inputs).

2) Liability cap: Recommend we offer a tiered cap tied to committed spend: 1x annual committed fees for general contract breaches; 2x for willful misconduct or gross negligence; unlimited for fraud or willful misconduct leading to bodily harm (standard carve-outs). This maps to Ben's placeholder.

3) Order Form/SLA: I tightened the SLA credits language and added a region-specific p95 table. Also added a short transitional clause: if Atlas chooses regional deployment in eu-west, metrics and remedies will be adjusted to reflect cross-border redundancy and data residency obligations.

I attached redline snippets for Exhibit C and the training addendum. Happy to join the call Thu 9:30am PT to walk Atlas legal through the language.

Attached: Redwood_Legal_QA_v1.docx (redline snippets)

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
